_licence.source: Runcible curated keyboard facts, written for this Book
_licence.note: Every row states where a key sits on a piano keyboard. A key's position is a fact of the instrument, not a passage of anybody's prose, which is why this file is authored rather than declared: no corpus publishes it and there is nothing here to attribute. musictheory.net and Hoffman Academy teach the same facts and neither grants a licence, so nothing of theirs is copied and both stay links in the chapters.

title: The twelve keys of one octave, by where they sit

fields.name: what the key is called. The answer a drill asks for, so it is a plain string.
fields.position: where the key is, said without naming another key. The prompt.
fields.pc: 0 for C up to 11 for B, so a drawn keyboard needs no lookup table.
fields.note: one line the drill can show after the answer.

white.name: C
white.position: the white key just to the left of a pair of black keys
white.note: C is the anchor. Find the pair of black keys anywhere on the instrument and C is immediately left of it.

white.name: D
white.position: the white key between the two black keys of a pair
white.note: D sits inside the pair, so it is the one white key with a black key on each side and nothing but the pair around it.

white.name: E
white.position: the white key just to the right of a pair of black keys
white.note: E closes the pair. C left, D inside, E right.

white.name: F
white.position: the white key just to the left of a group of three black keys
white.note: F opens the group of three the way C opens the pair.

white.name: G
white.position: the white key between the first and second black keys of a group of three
white.note: G and A are the two white keys buried inside the group of three.

white.name: A
white.position: the white key between the second and third black keys of a group of three
white.note: A is the second of the two white keys inside the group of three.

white.name: B
white.position: the white key just to the right of a group of three black keys
white.note: B closes the group of three, and the next white key to the right is C again.

black.name: C sharp or D flat
black.position: the lower of the two black keys in a pair
black.note: One key, two names. It is C sharp when it is a raised C and D flat when it is a lowered D, and which one is printed depends on the key the music is in.

black.name: D sharp or E flat
black.position: the upper of the two black keys in a pair
black.note: E flat is the name you meet first, because it belongs to the flat keys a beginner plays in.

black.name: F sharp or G flat
black.position: the lowest of the three black keys in a group
black.note: F sharp is the single sharp of G major, which is why it is the first black key most players learn by name.

black.name: G sharp or A flat
black.position: the middle of the three black keys in a group
black.note: The middle key of the three, and the only black key with a black key on both sides.

black.name: A sharp or B flat
black.position: the highest of the three black keys in a group
black.note: B flat is the single flat of F major, and it is spelled B flat far more often than A sharp.
